title: Before you start
tagline: What Git is, the five core words, how teams work, hosting sites, CI/CD, the terminal
description: No typing yet. Six short reads that explain what Git is for, the words everyone uses, how real teams work every day, and how this platform works, so the labs make sense from the first command.

title: Your first days at Ledgerly
tagline: Set up your machine, make your first saves, choose what to save, read history, keep secrets out
description: You just joined Ledgerly, a small company that makes invoicing software. These are sandbox labs — everything runs here in your browser, nothing can break. One idea at a time: set up Git, save your work, pick what goes into each save, look back through history, and keep passwords and junk out of it.

title: Building a feature with the team
tagline: Branches, combining work, conflicts with a teammate, parking work for an urgent fix
description: Still in the sandbox. Ledgerly needs a new feature: letting customers export their invoices. You will build it on your own branch (a safe side copy), combine it back with everyone else's work, sort out a clash when you and a teammate change the same thing, and learn how to drop a task when something urgent comes in.

title: Working with the team on GitHub
tagline: Share your work online, handle rejected pushes, open and respond to a pull request
description: Now it gets real. Up to here everything ran in your browser. In this track you move to GitHub — the website teams actually use to share code. It starts with one sandbox warm-up, then switches to Real mode, where you work in a real repository we set up for you. Real-mode steps need a free GitHub account and run on your own computer or in a browser-based workspace; the setup lab walks you through it, step by step.

title: Tidying history before you share it
tagline: Cherry-pick a fix to a release, and the one rule that keeps rewriting safe
description: Sometimes you need to reshape commits before anyone sees them, or copy one fix to another branch. This track covers the safe moves — starting with getting a single fix onto a shipped release — and the golden rule: only rewrite history that nobody else has.

title: When things go wrong
tagline: Get back lost commits, and safely undo a bad change on a shared branch
description: The reassuring track. Almost nothing you commit is ever truly lost — you just need to know where to look. Recover a commit you thought a reset destroyed, and undo a bad change on `main` the safe way, without breaking anyone else's copy.

title: How teams ship, at scale
tagline: Cut a release on real GitHub; branch protection, hotfixes and code owners
description: Real-mode again. The workflows teams use to ship safely: cut a tagged release with notes, and (coming next) hotfix while main has unreleased work, merge under branch-protection rules, and route reviews with CODEOWNERS.

title: Capstones
tagline: Sprint week, incident night, open source contributor
description: Multi-step, timed scenarios with bot teammates and minimal hints, pulling every track together.
